slides.1.title: Lisbon's Three Treasures: DOC Regional Map
slides.1.description: Bucelas (Arinto on limestone uplands), Colares (old-vine Ramisco on dunes), Carcavelos (rare fortified sweet white): three rare historic DOCs on the outskirts of Lisbon
slides.3.title: Bucelas: Guardian of High-Acid Arinto Whites
slides.3.html:
Bucelas DOC is one of Portugal's most important historic white wine DOCs, famous for high-acid whites from the Arinto variety.

📜 History

  • Became a legally defined region in 1911 (one of Portugal's earliest DOCs)
  • A favourite of the British market in the 17th-19th centuries, brought to Europe by the Duke of Wellington
  • Located about 30 km north of Lisbon, on limestone soils

🍋 The appeal of Arinto

  • Rules: Bucelas DOC whites must contain at least 75% Arinto
  • Limestone soils give minerality and a structural backbone
  • High acidity (pH 3.0-3.2); can age for 5-15 years
  • Style: fresh lime, white grapefruit and minerality, with a slightly bitter finish

🏆 Leading producers

  • Quinta da Murta: a benchmark for Bucelas, an Arinto purist
  • Quinta de Sant'Ana: organic farming, single-vineyard Arinto
slides.4.title: Colares: The Endangered Living Fossil of the Dunes
slides.4.html:
Colares DOC is one of the most endangered wine regions in Portugal, and even the world, yet it also has one of the most unique terroirs on earth.

🪨 Dunes and ungrafted old vines

  • Vines are planted in Atlantic coastal dunes (desert-like sand)
  • Phylloxera cannot survive in sand → Colares vines have never been grafted
  • Truly old vines of 100-200 years, some over 300 years
  • Yields per vine are extremely low (no more than 1-2 bottles of wine)

🍷 The Ramisco variety

  • Colares reds use Ramisco, a native variety found only here
  • High acidity and high tannin, with sea-salt breeze and rusty mineral notes; harsh when young
  • After ageing (10-30 years) it shows a one-of-a-kind salty sea breeze, leather and earth

⚠️ Endangered today

  • In the second half of the 20th century, heavy seaside resort construction cut vineyard area from 4,000 hectares to under 20 hectares
  • Only a handful of producers still make Colares DOC (best known: the Viúva Gomes cooperative, António Bernardino)
  • These wines are genuinely endangered: annual production may be just a few thousand bottles
slides.5.title: Lisbon's Three Treasures: Bucelas / Colares / Carcavelos Compared
slides.5.items.0.desc: High-acid Arinto whites, limestone, fresh and mineral, able to age for 15 years. Portugal's most important historic white wine DOC
slides.5.items.1.desc: Ungrafted old-vine Ramisco on dunes, salty-sea minerality, the rarest in the world, tiny production, now a collectors' treasure
slides.5.items.2.desc: Off-dry fortified wine (similar to Sherry), once exported to Britain, now almost extinct; only Quinta dos Pesos still produces it
slides.6.question: Why have Colares vines never needed grafting (they still use own-rooted vines)?
slides.6.options.1: Phylloxera cannot survive in the dune sand
slides.6.options.3: The climate is too cool for phylloxera to reproduce
slides.6.explanation: Colares vines are planted in the deep sand (dunes) of the Atlantic coast. Phylloxera cannot survive or spread in loose sand, so Colares vines were never affected by the 19th-century phylloxera epidemic and kept their ungrafted own-rooted old vines.
slides.7.question: What is the main grape variety of Bucelas DOC, and what is the minimum percentage required?
slides.7.explanation: Bucelas DOC requires whites to contain at least 75% Arinto. Arinto performs outstandingly on Bucelas's limestone soils, showing freshness, high acidity and minerality, and Bucelas is one of Portugal's most important historic white wine DOCs.
slides.8.title: Lisbon's Three Treasures: Additional Rules
slides.8.html:
Three DOCs close to the capital, with shrinking vineyard areas:

  • Colares: reds must contain ≥ 80% Ramisco and whites ≥ 80% Malvasia, both from ungrafted old vines on sandy ground, traditionally planted in trenches to resist the sea wind; reds from the firmer inland chão rijo soils must contain ≥ 80% Castelão
  • Carcavelos: only about 25 hectares remain. Reds must contain ≥ 75% Castelão and Preto Martinho; the wine is first fermented dry, then fortified and sweetened with vinho abafado (grape must whose fermentation is stopped with spirit), with ≥ 2 years in cask and ≥ 6 months in bottle
  • Bucelas: whites must contain ≥ 75% Arinto

Based on compiled data from 2011-2012.
slides.9.message: Congratulations on completing the Lisbon's Three Treasures lesson!
slides.9.keyPoints.0: Bucelas: high-acid Arinto whites, limestone, 75% Arinto required by regulation, can age for 15 years
slides.9.keyPoints.1: Colares: ungrafted old-vine Ramisco on dunes, the rarest in the world; phylloxera cannot survive in sand
slides.9.keyPoints.2: Carcavelos: off-dry fortified wine, now almost extinct, with only one producer left
slides.9.keyPoints.3: All three are historic areas on Lisbon's outskirts, living fossils of Portuguese wine
